extracted.intended_audience: FERC commissioners and staff, CEQ, EPA, PHMSA, pipeline/project developers, electric utility regulatory/legal staff, and other agency policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Drafting or evaluating formal industry comments to FERC/CEQ on NEPA treatment of greenhouse gas emissions and the Commission's certificate policy for interstate natural gas facilities; focuses on legal adequacy, methodology, interagency coordination, and practical implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with statutory authority (NGA) and NEPA procedural obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Any action the Commission takes must be consistent with its authority under the Natural Gas Act (NGA) and the procedural obligations imposed by the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission must carefully analyze its statutory authority because the NGA does not provide direct enumerated authority to regulate environmental performance; environmental analysis derives from NEPA, which is procedural. Ensure that measures rest within statutory authority and do not conflict with other agencies' statutory authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robust NEPA GHG analyses with proper contextualization
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission’s GHG analyses under NEPA should be robust and provide proper contextualization of emissions to allow for a complete assessment of potential emissions impacts from proposed infrastructure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify reasonably foreseeable emissions where appropriate, but contextualize and caveat such quantifications. Contextualization can include sector-wide trends and comparisons (e.g., project emissions vs. sector or national emissions) to aid in legal sufficiency and informed decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case-by-case foreseeability of upstream and downstream emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether upstream and downstream emissions are ‘reasonably foreseeable effects’ must be determined on a case-by-case basis consistent with D.C. Circuit precedent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow D.C. Circuit tests (e.g., Sabal Trail, Birckhead, Food & Water Watch) — foreseeability depends on specificity about destination and end use of the gas. Do not treat downstream emissions as categorically foreseeable; evaluate information about where gas is going and how it will be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider applicant-provided evidence of net-reductions and low-/no-carbon fuel use
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission should include consideration of record evidence of net-reductions in GHG emissions where the transported gas would displace higher-emitting fuels or enable emerging low- or no-emissions fuels (e.g., hydrogen).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If project proponents supply reasonable evidence that a facility will reduce sector emissions or allow transport of low-/no-carbon fuels, the Commission should consider those claims and contextualize them in NEPA analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sector-wide contextualization and assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Sector-wide assessments of total GHG emissions and emissions trends can help understand direct, indirect, and cumulative impacts of a proposed action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use available sector-wide analyses to place project emissions in context, especially for projects implicating electricity generation. Sector assessments can substitute for precise quantification when quantifying emissions is difficult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative assessments where quantification is difficult
rubrics_metrics.description: Where GHG emissions are difficult to quantify, agencies should provide qualitative assessments informed by sector-wide analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on reliable, existing sector-wide studies to provide qualitative context instead of forcing speculative numerical estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for upstream methane reductions using industry-standard, identifiable methods
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission should ensure methane emissions are appropriately mitigated and require project developers to provide information using reasonably identifiable and quantifiable methods used throughout the industry today.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage use of voluntary industry initiatives (e.g., NGSI) and consistent measurement practices; require information consistent with current industry methods to ensure analyses are legally sufficient and defensible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deference to EPA (and PHMSA as appropriate) on sufficiency of emissions mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission should defer to EPA regarding environmental risk analysis and the sufficiency of emissions mitigation measures, given EPA’s Clean Air Act jurisdiction and expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid crafting mitigation requirements that conflict with EPA actions; consult and coordinate to prevent inconsistent or duplicative standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interagency coordination to avoid duplication and inconsistent requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission should collaborate with sister agencies (EPA, PHMSA, CEQ) on GHG issues within its jurisdiction to avoid duplication and conflicting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with other federal agencies and consider deferring where those agencies have primary expertise/jurisdiction; align with Executive Order 14008 calls for coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit mitigation and conditions to Commission jurisdiction (avoid de facto denials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any mitigation measure or condition imposed must be within the Commission’s Section 7 jurisdiction and must not amount to a de facto denial of a certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attach conditions that indirectly accomplish what the Commission lacks direct power to require. Ensure conditions remain focused on certificate process and entities under Section 7 jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent and uniform application of policy statements
rubrics_metrics.description: While applying the Draft Updated Certificate Policy Statement and Draft GHG Policy Statement flexibly, the Commission must apply them in a reasonably consistent manner across cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniform application provides regulatory certainty, reduces litigation risk, and decreases investor uncertainty. Balance case-by-case analysis with consistent methods and expectations for applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain efficient review processes and evidentiary grounding
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission must maintain efficient review processes and ensure decisions remain reasoned and grounded in reliable evidence even when considering a broader range of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overly burdensome requirements that slow reviews; focus on reliability of evidence and reasoned explanation to withstand judicial review and avoid delays that impede clean energy projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tiering off prior analyses; do not reanalyze indirect effects already addressed
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should tier off prior environmental analyses and should not be required to reexamine indirect effects already analyzed or regulated in other proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 40 C.F.R. § 1502.20 (tiering) to avoid duplicative analyses. If emissions from a facility have already been assessed in permitting the facility, other agencies need not reanalyze those emissions as indirect effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA is procedural; GHG analysis is informational and should not itself dictate approval
rubrics_metrics.description: NEPA prescribes procedural steps for informed agency decision-making; NEPA does not mandate particular substantive outcomes, and GHG emissions alone should not drive NEPA decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NEPA analyses to inform the section 7 balancing test under the NGA, but recognize NEPA does not impose substantive mitigation obligations; agencies should not treat NEPA as a tool to impose substantive environmental performance beyond their authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution on use of global/regional climate models and downscaling for NEPA
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should be cautious in applying GCMs/RCMs and downscaling for regional/local NEPA analyses due to limitations, uncertainties, and resource demands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose uncertainties if models are used, avoid relying on speculative regional projections without adequate resources and expertise, and discourage burdensome modeling unless capacity and benefit justify it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid treating small project-level emissions as significant (25,000 tpy threshold critique)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not equate individual project emissions at or above 25,000 tons per year with a ‘significant effect’ requiring an EIS; 25,000 tpy is too low relative to nationwide/global emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that many projects' emissions are minuscule compared to global emissions; guidance should not require extensive qualitative discussion of a project's effect on climate change beyond publishing projected annual emissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit required discussion of project emissions' effect on climate to publication of projected annual levels
rubrics_metrics.description: Given attribution limitations, NEPA guidance should not require agencies to analyze or discuss how an individual project's emissions affect climate change qualitatively or quantitatively; instead publish projected annual emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where attribution to climate impacts is speculative, agencies should at most report projected emissions and avoid causal claims linking specific project emissions to discrete climate impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodic reassessment of modeling tools and limited scenario analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should periodically reassess the evolution of climate models and, for now, undertake only simple scenario analyses where useful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage agencies to monitor modeling advances and, until models are sufficiently robust at regional/local scales, limit modeling to modest scenario exercises to highlight monitoring needs rather than definitive predictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider applicant's purpose and reasonable alternatives in purpose-and-need statements
rubrics_metrics.description: It is appropriate to consider the applicant’s purposes when framing the purpose and need for a project and when defining the scope of reasonable alternatives under NEPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support flexibility that allows consideration of the applicant's objectives to shape alternatives analysis rather than imposing external constraints that could preclude reasonable alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance NEPA information requirements with inherent uncertainty in GHG quantification
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ and agencies should balance NEPA’s disclosure objectives with the practical difficulties and uncertainties in quantifying reasonably foreseeable direct and indirect GHG emissions for specific projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid requiring speculative quantifications; allow qualitative context or tiering where appropriate and ensure information requests are proportional to evidentiary value and agency expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrict mitigation/analysis obligations to entities and measures within Commission's jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Any analytical requirements or mitigation obligations imposed through the certificate process should be limited to entities and measures over which the Commission has authority under NGA Section 7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure focus on certificate-related issues and avoid imposing requirements on parties outside Commission jurisdiction or adopting mitigation regimes effectively enforced by other agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design NEPA analyses to withstand judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete, contextual NEPA analysis helps produce legally sufficient documents that will withstand D.C. Circuit review and reduce costly litigation delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear record, quantify and contextualize emissions where reasonable, explain methodology and caveats, and tie findings to precedent to reduce reversal risk under courts' case-by-case foreseeability tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage voluntary industry measurement and disclosure initiatives (NGSI) for consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Support voluntary industry-led efforts (e.g., Natural Gas Sustainability Initiative) to advance best practices and consistent methane emissions measurement and disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote industry-led standards to complement regulation, provide consistency and comparability across the supply chain, and improve the quality of emissions data used in NEPA analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt a holistic approach to GHG analysis under NEPA
rubrics_metrics.description: Place emissions in broader context (sector, trends, displacement effects) to buttress both NEPA analysis and the Commission’s obligations under NGA Section 7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use contextual and sector-wide information to show how a project may reduce indirect emissions (e.g., by enabling renewables integration) and to demonstrate net effects rather than isolated project figures.
